summary: Both editions were independently reviewed against all ten paragraphs of the selected working Greek. Both preserve the narrative, three appearances, speaker changes, required inquiry and fasting, receiving promise, bodily warning, sufficiency assertion, negatively framed question, and plural rebuke disclosed in the notes. The simplified edition introduces no concrete fidelity defect. The notes retain the selected working readings while distinguishing reported alternatives, corrections, and editorial intervention. Acceptance is limited to fidelity to the supplied source and disclosure of the supplied reports; it does not authenticate unseen manuscripts, independently verify editions or archival records, or certify exhaustive collation.
